Not for the participant repo. R and Python chunks in one document;
Python chunks run through the reticulate package.

```{r}
#| label: setup-data
library(reticulate)   # lets R-based Quarto docs run Python chunks
phones <- data.frame(Year = as.integer(rownames(WorldPhones)), WorldPhones,
                     row.names = NULL)
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(phones, "data/worldphones.csv", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
```

## Python: the same CSV and chart

```{python}
#| label: py-chart
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

phones = pd.read_csv("data/worldphones.csv")
phones.set_index("Year").plot(logy=True, title="Telephones by region (thousands)")
plt.show()
```

## Python: scrape with pandas (the easy way)

```{python}
#| label: py-scrape-pandas
import requests
from io import StringIO

url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_number_of_telephone_lines_in_use"
headers = {"User-Agent": "SIS-AI-Workshop/1.0 (educational use)"}
html = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=30).text

today = pd.read_html(StringIO(html), attrs={"class": "wikitable"})[0]
today.head()
```

## Python: what pandas is doing under the hood (Beautiful Soup)

```{python}
#| label: py-scrape-bs4
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
table = soup.find("table", class_="wikitable")

rows = []
for tr in table.find_all("tr")[1:]:
    cells = [td.get_text(strip=True) for td in tr.find_all(["td", "th"])]
    if cells:
        rows.append(cells)

rows[:5]
```
